items.note: Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra LVII.360: 'The sport of the Hamsas should be carved on the walls of the temple' (Deo Baloda example).
Plate XLIII caption: Udayapur, Gwalior, built by the Paramāra King Udayāditya.
Udayāditya given as c. 1059-1087 A.D. in the plate caption; temple of red sandstone.
Plan: widely projected bhadra in each main direction; other buttresses form right angles laid out within a circle.
Prāsādas with this plan are classified as Bhūmi-ja, 'country-born', said to be both square and circular in plan (Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra LXV).

claim.value: Bhūmi-ja plan, 'country-born', square and circular (S.S. LXV)

items.note: Pallavikā 'bud'-like buttresses with faceted apices dissolve the walls into light and shade; jaṅghā buttresses appear as pillars.
Footnote: the temple is also known as Udayeśvara Temple; ASIAR 1923-24 p. 133; Cunningham ASI Report X p. 65, VII p. 82 f.

items.note: Adhiṣṭhāna and vedikā mouldings at Udayapur resemble those of Khajuraho in name and shape but differ in effect through proportion and position.
Śikhara sealed by the śukanāsā in the East and by śukanāsikās of half its height in the other three quarters.
Pillared shrines at the pallavikā bases hold images of Parivāra-devatās such as Gaṇeśa and his female counterpart.
Vājana fillet with kīrttimukha and a heavy chain ending in a small bell in relief, on the wall as pillar.
Recessed planes hold a continuous panel with Śakti as Vana-devatā below a creeper carrying celestials and animals.
Śikhara base of a double zone of mouldings; flat latās with gavākṣa lattices spring from the śukanāsā; seven bhūmis of five śṛṅgas in each sub-quarter.
Skandha edge repeats the five-pointed star plan; āmalaka rim responds to the star-shaped temple; wall themes continue on the curvilinear śikhara.

Correspondence of structure and superstructure through the pillar theme is not particular to the Nilakaṇṭheśvara at Udayapur; Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra chapters on Nāgara and Vārāta Prāsādas prescribe it.
